title: Diwali in London 2026: Greenwich's Free Festival, Dishoom and the Feasts
excerpt: Diwali falls on November 8. The free National Maritime Museum day is November 7, Dishoom's headline nights are sold out, and Jamavar, Kutir and KOKUM feasts are still booking.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 in London this year, and most celebrations run from late October to November 8 — several headline events are already sold out.
  • The free anchor event is the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich on November 7: dance, rangoli, lantern-making, a new Diwali Bazaar and a lantern parade through Greenwich Park.
  • Dishoom's Borough house party on November 5 and its Vikas Khanna supper clubs on November 3 (Shoreditch) and November 4 (Canary Wharf) are sold out; its workshops and storytelling sessions on November 6-8 are the remaining route in — book through Dishoom's events page.
  • Restaurant feasts still booking include Jamavar's Diwali Darbar (October 28-November 8, £138) and Kutir's seven-course menus in Chelsea (November 2-8, £80).

London's Diwali calendar this year is built around one date — Sunday, November 8 — and a fortnight of events leading up to it. The roundup by London The Inside and the listings at Secret London agree on the shape of the season: restaurant feasts from late October, a free museum takeover in Greenwich, and fireworks that share the weekend with Bonfire Night.

The free day out: Greenwich, November 7

The National Maritime Museum's Diwali day is free and family-oriented: dance performances, rangoli art, lantern-making and traditional clothing to try on, with South Asian artists, storytellers and community organisations taking over the museum. New for 2026 is a Diwali Bazaar selling jewellery, prints, clothing and handmade pieces from South Asian designers and independent businesses. The day ends with a lantern parade through Greenwich Park, led by Eternal Taal's dhol drummers. In Harrow, the Byron Park fireworks on November 7 combine a Bonfire Night display with Diwali dance performances and a funfair beforehand.

"New for 2026 is a Diwali Bazaar selling jewellery, prints, clothing and handmade pieces from South Asian designers and independent businesses."

Dishoom: sold out at the top, open at the edges

Dishoom's new Borough café is the hub of its programme, with a neon installation by artist Chila Kumari Singh Burman MBE outside until the end of December. The November 5 house party — mehendi, photo booths, a DJ — is sold out, as are the two supper clubs with New York chef Vikas Khanna of Bungalow: Shoreditch on November 3 and Canary Wharf on November 4, built around dishes including Bungalow's spice-roasted pineapple curry alongside Dishoom's black daal. What remains bookable at the time of the listings: Borough workshops on November 6-8, including chai and conversation with co-founder Kavi Thakrar (£5), a zine-making workshop (£35) and family storytelling with children's author Chitra Soundar on November 8 for ages 4-9.

Feasts worth booking now

Jamavar in Mayfair, marking its 10th anniversary, serves a Diwali Darbar feast at £138 per person from October 28 to November 8, modelled on princely-court celebrations, with Old Delhi butter chicken and Hampshire lamb achari gosht. The Ambassadors Clubhouse feast menu, Punjabi in inspiration, is £120 per person from October 26 to November 15. In Chelsea, Rohit Ghai's Kutir runs seven-course signature and vegetarian expedition menus from November 2 to 8 at £80 per person, with wine pairing at £55. KOKUM in East Dulwich serves a limited-edition sharing feast from November 3 to 8, and Haldiram's in Leicester Square is running a Diwali sweet counter through the festive period, including rose ladoo and badam kesar launj alongside standard mithai. Vivek Singh's Cinnamon Collection restaurants serve multi-course Diwali feasts from October 19 to November 14.

Planning notes

Three practical points emerge from the listings. First, the ticketed headline events went first — anything Dishoom-led should be treated as waitlist-only. Second, the free Greenwich day on November 7 is the strongest family option and needs no booking for the museum programme itself. Third, Diwali day itself, November 8, is comparatively quiet in the listings, because most venues front-load the preceding weekend; readers who want a Diwali-day meal should book the restaurant feasts, several of which run through November 8, rather than expect a major public event that Sunday.
